Rendered page visually inspected; Afghan regional comparator.

Native formulas/indexing differ from OpenLogic; preserve source formulas exactly. Rendered page visually inspected; Afghan regional comparator.

A translator note gives even and odd natural numbers as an example of a two-part partition, explicitly using جفت and طاق. It supports parity vocabulary only; the surrounding order-theory discussion is not credited to the current section.

Native school mathematics explicitly distinguishes base, exponent, and the resulting power expression with قاعده, توان ښودونکی, and طاقت. Supports the pairing-formula explanation; no source formula is imported.

anchor: د کانتور د قطر پر طریقه
evidence_note: Introduces uncountable real numbers, explicitly contrasts countable and uncountable sets, names Cantor and the diagonal method, and begins a proof by contradiction from an assumed enumeration. Strong native concept-specific prose; its decimal-real proof is not substituted for OpenLogic binary-sequence or power-set proofs.

anchor: د قطر د طریقې څخه کار اخلو
evidence_note: Completes a decimal diagonal contradiction and then constructs h(k)=f_k(k)+1 to show that any countable family of natural-number sequences omits a sequence. Supports diagonal construction and contradiction language. Different index base and digit-changing rule remain source-specific and are not imported.

anchor: د سیټ بوج سره مساوی دی
evidence_note: Uses a bijection between naturals and even naturals to state equality of set sizes, then proves reflexivity by identity, symmetry by inverse, and transitivity by composition. Direct concept-specific evidence for equinumerosity as an equivalence relation. The witness uses بوج/equal cardinality rather than the edition adjective همشمېره and reverses composition notation, so only its language and proof structure are adopted.

anchor: بوج کوچنی او یا مساوي دی
evidence_note: Defines cardinal size no greater than by an injection and strict cardinal inequality by injection without equal cardinality, then gives subset and interval examples. Direct concept-specific evidence for cardinal comparison; the edition keeps OpenLogic cardle/cardless notation and Pakistani phrasing.

States Cantor’s theorem |X|<|P(X)|, gives the singleton injection, and starts the diagonal contradiction with E={x in X: x notin f(x)}. Direct native proof witness. Its controller analogy, notation and composition conventions are not copied into OpenLogic.

States Cantor–Bernstein: injections/cardinal inequalities in both directions imply equal cardinality, and begins a piecewise bijection proof. Direct native theorem witness. OpenLogic defers its proof, so the edition does not import this witness proof or claim it as translated source content.

Proves that square root of two is irrational by an infinite-descent/parity argument, then introduces interval notation and asks for lower-bound and infimum definitions. Direct native witness for real, rational/irrational, square-root, bound and infimum prose. Its proof and notation are comparator evidence only; OpenLogic controls its two separate source proofs.

Uses supremum notation for a bounded set of reals, states density of the rationals, and distinguishes rational from irrational real numbers. Direct regional concept evidence for least-upper-bound and real-number language; the exact Pakistani surface remains provisional.

anchor: تبادلي خاصيت / اتحادي خاصيت / توزيعي خاصيت
evidence_note: States commutative and associative laws for addition and multiplication and the distributive law, with formulas. Direct regional technical witness for these operation properties. It does not define rings or fields, so those structure labels remain provisional.

Names the Bolzano-Cauchy principle, describes every real-number sequence as having a limit in that historical summary, and connects the principle with the construction of real-number theory. Direct regional evidence for the historical and limit vocabulary; OpenLogic controls the rational Cauchy-sequence definition and its quantifiers.

Introduces real-number sequences, defines a limit with epsilon and a natural-number threshold, and labels a sequence with a limit convergent or approaching. Direct native concept evidence for sequence, limit and convergence prose. Its domain is the reals, so the edition preserves OpenLogic’s rational-valued Cauchy definition instead.

anchor: د رياضي د استقراء په هکله
evidence_note: States mathematical induction for a property of every natural number: the property holds at zero and preservation from n to n+1 yields the universal conclusion. It also proves the principle through the set of naturals satisfying the property. Direct regional concept and proof-language evidence; OpenLogic controls its Dedekind-algebra generalization.

Names an order isomorphism as a bijection whose inverse also preserves order and describes isomorphic structures. Direct regional evidence for the isomorphism label and preservation idea; it is an order-specific witness, so the Dedekind-algebra signature remains source-controlled.

anchor: د ډدیکینډ پر اساس د متناهي سیټ
evidence_note: Discusses finiteness in Dedekind’s sense and proves, using Choice, that a nonfinite set has the same cardinality as a proper subset obtained by removing one point from an injected copy of the naturals. Direct regional concept evidence for Dedekind finite/infinite and proper-subset equinumerosity; OpenLogic’s injection formulation governs the definition.

anchor: د طبيعي عددونو د سټ جوړول
evidence_note: Constructs the naturals as a set containing zero, closed under the successor operation x union singleton x, and included in every set with those two properties. It explicitly connects this minimality property with proof by mathematical induction. Direct native concept evidence for successor closure and the least closed set.

anchor: د حقيقت د جدول Truth Table
evidence_note: Uses 1 and 0 for truth and falsity, names a truth table, defines negation, and begins the definition of conjunction. Direct regional evidence for truth-value, truth-table and connective concepts; the Pakistani edition adapts spelling and uses its own consistent labels.

anchor: د بيان الجبر د انشاء لړ
evidence_note: Defines a finite propositional formation sequence: each entry is atomic, the negation of an earlier entry, or the result of applying a binary connective to earlier entries; a formula is the last entry of such a sequence. Direct regional concept evidence for formation sequences and formula construction; OpenLogic controls the exact grammar and metasyntactic notation.

anchor: د بيان په سيټ کښې صدق کوي
evidence_note: Defines semantic validity of an argument by requiring the conclusion to have value 1 in every joint truth-table row where all premises have value 1, and uses the semantic turnstile. Direct regional concept evidence for satisfaction and entailment; the edition uses valuation-based definitions and preserves OpenLogic notation.

Defines a tautology as a formula whose truth-table value is 1 in every row and relates this to semantic consequence from the empty premise set. Direct regional evidence for the tautology concept and its connection with entailment; Pakistani spelling is normalized in the edition.

Defines semantic consequence using every mapping from propositional variables to 0 and 1, then defines feasibility by the existence of such a mapping making every premise and the formula true. It also relates entailment of a formula to infeasibility of its negation. Direct regional concept evidence for valuation semantics and satisfiability; OpenLogic definitions govern the exact scope and the edition uses a clearer satisfiable label.

anchor: د بيان د الجبر د اکسيومي
evidence_note: States a proof of a tautology-preservation result and then lists propositional axiom schemas. Direct regional evidence for proof and axiom vocabulary and for formula-shaped axioms; the edition preserves each OpenLogic calculus rather than importing this particular axiom list.

anchor: د استنباط د قوانينو د سټ
evidence_note: Defines a mathematical theory using a countable sign set, well-formed statements, axioms and a finite set of inference relations; it then defines a proof as a statement sequence whose entries are logical axioms, theory axioms or modus-ponens consequences. Direct regional concept evidence for axiom schemas, inference rules and proof sequences.

Displays modus ponens as an inference rule and proves its admissibility in an arbitrary theory by concatenating two proof sequences and appending the conclusion. Direct regional evidence for the rule name, inference-rule presentation and derivability argument; OpenLogic controls its own derivation formats.
